<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**35** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 68e726d631132db46fd63b887f15927ac3b9b5c3`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 68e726d631132db46fd63b887f15927ac3b9b5c3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d2abce3f52af5dc2c071e670671c513e45915e80` — the merge of head `999b09d9c3724b90db62df71dfb52afcf73ec569` into base `68e726d631132db46fd63b887f15927ac3b9b5c3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d2abce3f52af5dc2c071e670671c513e45915e80 && git checkout d2abce3f52af5dc2c071e670671c513e45915e80
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 68e726d631132db46fd63b887f15927ac3b9b5c3 999b09d9c3724b90db62df71dfb52afcf73ec569 && git checkout -B drift-repro 68e726d631132db46fd63b887f15927ac3b9b5c3 && git merge --no-ff 999b09d9c3724b90db62df71dfb52afcf73ec569

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 68e726d631132db46fd63b887f15927ac3b9b5c3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 68e726d631132db46fd63b887f15927ac3b9b5c3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `999b09d9c3724b90db62df71dfb52afcf73ec569`
Area: S4 / E1 · Fixes #33851 · ordinary ACCEPT read per review-checklist.md. No contract face: no `packages/spec/src`, no governed path, and no narrowing arm.

1. **Premise measured.** Red before each half: §3's 3 write-through fault cases answered `success: true` on `63e47feeca`, and §4's 3 heal-stop cases did the same on `2d23b49dd1`.
   - Ablations A1–A5 and B1–B3 each turn the named cases red and were restored to blob == HEAD.
   - A4 and A5 prove that the save and publish controls would catch a leaked answer.
2. **Mechanism, read on the tree.**
   - `answerFaults` is set in two places only: `revertCommit`'s restore limb, and the heal's remaining-row loop.
   - The heal answers a `RegistryHealStop` from its outer catch and from its first remaining-row refusal, and its `error` line is kept.
   - The soft-remove limb reads the stop only when `current` holds, that is, when a row was actually removed.
   - I listed every caller of `restoreArtifactRegistryView` in `packages/**`. Besides `revertCommit` there are 11: delete-load ×3, publish ×3, batch registration, class-head, packageless migration, hydration ×2. Each one awaits and discards the answer, so delete, publish undo and convergence keep their answers.
   - `rollbackToPackageCommit` reaches it through `host.revertCommit`, so the changeset's sentence about rollback holds.
3. **Clause-② no, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch`: right.** `RegistryHealStop` and `RegistryWriteThroughRequest` are not re-exported from `src/index.ts`, and the forwarders that use them are private. What changes is `revertCommit` answering truthfully under ADR-0067 D3 for every type. #33805 already made that move for objects, so this is not a narrowing. Dogfood is n/a because the PR has no `!` and no narrowing arm.
4. **Tests.**
   - §3 (12 cases) and §4 (9 cases) are top-level describes in the shared revert harness, as AGENTS.md ruling 6583487846 requires.
   - Each fault case asserts `success: false`, the `failed[0]` type, name and `code` (`NOT_OVERRIDABLE`), and the row-state text.
   - The controls assert the unchanged `warn` and `error` lines.
5. **Changeset.** Each sentence matches the diff. The #33563 note is untouched here, and its one-sentence correction rides #34017 (`Part of #33851`), which must land after this PR.
6. **Lane line.** Claim 6895262027 says "no `protocol.ts`", but the head edits two private forwarders and one docblock in it. That is allowed under the 14:41Z/14:45Z rule change, as on #33885. Amend the claim to name `protocol.ts` before ACCEPT.
7. **Overlap.** I checked `git merge-tree --write-tree` myself: clean against `origin/main` and against #33885's current head `e516f353`, not only the `fa7fb66a7c` the body cites.
8. **Out-of-scope finding.** The heal's object-owner `unregisterObject` refusal is still only a `warn` line. It is listed under Acceptance notes and marked "noted, not filed". The seat decides whether to file it, record it as an accepted deviation, or drop it, and writes that outcome in the ACCEPT.
9. **Check-runs on the head:** 36 success, 18 skipped, and one in progress, a re-run of `Check Changeset` started 16:21Z after the body edit (its earlier run on this head succeeded). Lint & Repo Gates, every Type Check lane, Test Core 1–8/8, Build Core and the Dogfood Regression Gate are all green. Arm once the `Check Changeset` re-run is green.
